questions.text: Two machines, P and Q, share one link of rate R bps. They sit d meters apart and the signal travels along the link at v meters/sec. P sends Q a frame of F bits. How long does the frame take to arrive at Q?
Give reasons to prefer TCP/IP over UDP/IP when a file has to be moved between two hosts.
List the building blocks of a data communication system.
Distinguish the TCP receive window from the maximum segment size.
Define FQDN and PQDN, with one example of each.

A user types a site name into a browser. Before any page request can be sent, the name must be turned into an IP address. Describe each step of that lookup, from the user's host to the moment the address comes back.
Define persistent and non-persistent HTTP connections. Show an example of each on a timeline diagram.
Describe how a client and a server open a TCP connection, exchange data and then close the connection.

Node A must deliver a message of 9 packets to node B over a sliding window of size 3 with Go-Back-N recovery. Every packet is ready from the start. Every 5th packet that A transmits is lost, while no acknowledgement from B is ever lost. How many packets does A transmit in all? Support your answer with a transition diagram.

A Stop-and-Wait ARQ link runs at 1 Mbps and one bit needs 20 milliseconds for a round trip. (i) Find the bandwidth-delay product. (ii) With data packets of 1,000 bits, find the link utilization percentage under Stop-and-Wait. (iii) If up to 15 packets may be sent before an acknowledgement is required (as in Go-Back-N ARQ), find the utilization percentage.

A TCP header is captured in hexadecimal as E29300170000000100000000500207FF.... From it read the source port, destination port, sequence number, acknowledgement number, header length, segment type and window size.
Write short notes on any two of the following. (i) Network topologies
Write short notes on any two of the following. (ii) The Simple Mail Transfer Protocol
Write short notes on any two of the following. (iii) Congestion control in TCP
State the key distinction between a fully qualified and a partially qualified domain name. What is a CNAME record used for?
A UDP header is shown in hexadecimal: 0045 DF00 0058 0000. Give the source and destination port numbers and the length of the data, and say whether the sender computed a checksum.
In stop-and-wait every 4th packet is lost and 15 (fifteen) packets must be delivered. How many transmissions are needed in all?
A server has the domain name www.example.edu. Write the HTTP request that retrieves the document /usr/users/doc. The client accepts MIME version 1 and GIF or JPEG images.
How many sequence numbers does each of these TCP segments use up? (i) SYN (ii) ACK (iii) SYN+ACK (iv) Data

A browser sends an HTTP request to a web server. The server answers by opening a TCP connection, which takes 8.4 milliseconds (ms) including the RTT. The browser then asks for the site's index file, which refers to 22 (twenty two) more images that the browser must fetch. Taking all other conditions as equal, how much longer does non-persistent HTTP take than persistent HTTP?
Describe each of these e-mail concepts: (i) the architecture of an e-mail system, (ii) the phases of mail transfer, (iii) a message access agent, (iv) MIME (Multipurpose Internet Mail Extension).

Explain how the different packet delays are computed, and say which of them are constant and which vary. Then find the total time to transfer a 1.5MB file, given: the bandwidth is 10Mbps; after each data packet the sender waits one RTT before sending the next; the RTT is 80 ms; a packet carries 1 KB of data; and an initial 2×RTT of handshaking precedes the data.
Draw the TCP header format and briefly describe each field.

Derive how the window size relates to the sequence-number space in Go-Back-N (GBN) and Selective Repeat (SR). With three-bit sequence numbers, find the window size for each. Using a neat diagram for each, show what goes wrong when the window exceeds the value you found.

Node A must send a message of nine (9) packets to node B with a sliding window of size 3 and Go-Back-N (GBN) recovery. All packets are available at once. Every 5th packet that A transmits is lost, but no acknowledgement from B is ever lost. How many packets does A transmit to deliver the message?

A TCP connection starts with initial sequence number 2171. The client opens it, sends three segments (the second carrying 1000 bytes of data) and then closes the connection. Give the sequence number of each segment the client sends: (i) the SYN segment (ii) the data segment (iii) the FIN segment.
List the TCP states and give the TCP state transition diagram.

Host M has 9 packets for host N and uses a sliding window of size 3 with Go-Back-N error control. All packets are ready at once. Every 5th packet that M sends is lost, and no acknowledgement from N is lost. How many packets does M send in total?
Which minimum set of functions must a transport protocol add to what the network protocol already provides?
A client sends 16 bytes of data in a UDP datagram. Calculate the transmission efficiency at the UDP level.
Which resource record type holds the canonical name of a host?
In client-server computing, why must the server stay on all the time while a client may come and go?

Describe each field of the TCP header, with a header figure. A TCP segment is 1 KB long, its header length value is 6 and its sequence number is 3500. The URG flag is 1 and the URG pointer is 45. How many bytes are urgent, and what are their sequence numbers?
Caching shortens the time to download an object but can serve an out-of-date copy. How does HTTP deal with this stale-copy problem?
DNS may run over UDP or over TCP. Explain when UDP is the better choice and when TCP is.

Both directions use a 1000-byte maximum segment size (MSS). The client numbers its bytes from ISN 50 and the server from ISN 81. The client has 2000 bytes to send and the server has 3000 bytes. Give the full exchange of segments; for each one draw an arrow labelled with its SYN, ACK and FIN bits and its SEQ and ACK values. Assume nothing is lost and that applications read data the moment it arrives.
Explain, with a flow diagram, how stop-and-wait copes with a lost packet and with a lost acknowledgement.
A stop-and-wait link has a 1 Mbps line and needs 20 ms to carry one bit there and back. Compute the bandwidth-delay product, then the link utilization percentage for data packets of 1,000 bits.
Write brief notes on any two of these: (a) circuit-switched versus packet-switched networks.
Write brief notes on any two of these: (b) multiplexing versus demultiplexing.
Write brief notes on any two of these: (c) slow start versus additive increase in congestion control.
